routes.label: Solve the head and leg totals

question: The Fort Worth Zoo has a number of two-legged birds and a number of four-legged mammals. On one visit to the zoo, Margie counted \(200\) heads and \(522\) legs. How many of the animals that Margie counted were two-legged birds?
solution:
The \(200\) heads mean there are \(200\) animals. If all were birds, they would have \(200\cdot2=400\) legs.

Replacing one imagined bird with a mammal keeps the animal count unchanged and adds \(4-2=2\) legs. The actual count has \(522-400=122\) extra legs, so there must be
\[
122\div2=61
\]
mammals. The remaining \(200-61=139\) animals are birds. Indeed, \(2\cdot139+4\cdot61=522\), as required. There are \(\boxed{139}\) birds, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
